answer: A concrete defense is a three-party interlock per task. The requester hashes its specification; graders are sampled from five disjoint shards; an escrow pays only when four of five match that hash. Nobody learns the others in advance, so a cluster must hold all five shards to self-deal, a (s/N)^5 probability that collapses as the network grows. Collusion surfaces as a hollow echo of one voice, and the escrow burns the offender's bond. Facing a gale of random draws, a farm must spread across clean identities, turning its harbor of fakes into a cost center, not a moat.
